blocks.text: A reusable Vue 3 component library by Saqif Hoque. Install the package in your own application, connect your data, and shape the surrounding interface however you need.

items: Real component, not an iframe or a hosted service.
ES module package, styles, and public TypeScript declarations.
Live examples use the published npm package, not a source-code alias.

blocks.text: npm install @saqif/vue-dicom-canvas vue@^3.5.0 dwv@~0.36.4
Use the navigation to get started, open the playground, or look up individual props. These docs cover npm version 2.0.1.

pages.title: Installation
pages.lead: Add the package to an existing Vue 3 application.

blocks.text: npm install @saqif/vue-dicom-canvas "vue@^3.5.0" "dwv@~0.36.4"
Import the component and its CSS once in your application. Vue is a peer dependency; keep a single compatible Vue instance.

import { DicomViewer } from '@saqif/vue-dicom-canvas'
import '@saqif/vue-dicom-canvas/style.css'
DICOM Canvas also needs decoder worker assets. Complete the Worker setup guide before using compressed studies.

blocks.text: Kebab-case is used in templates: workerBasePath becomes worker-base-path.

pages.title: Worker setup
pages.lead: Serve decoder workers from the same origin as your app.

blocks.text:
mkdir -p public/assets/workers
cp node_modules/@saqif/vue-dicom-canvas/workers/*.min.js public/assets/workers/

<DicomViewer :source="source"
  worker-base-path="/assets/workers/" />
Keep all six packaged worker files. These runtime assets are required for supported decoding paths; they are not demo code.
For subpath deployments, use a document-relative worker-base-path such as ./assets/workers/. Every mounted viewer must use the same worker directory.
A missing worker, HTML fallback response, incorrect base path, or cross-origin URL can prevent decoding. Listen to worker-error to identify the resolved URL.

pages.title: Files & remote URLs
pages.lead: Load files, series, or an authenticated imaging endpoint.

blocks.text:
<DicomViewer :source="source"
  :remote-request-options="{
    headers: [{ name: 'Authorization', value: `Bearer ${token}` }],
    withCredentials: false,
    batchSize: 4
  }"
  worker-base-path="/assets/workers/" />

The remote server must allow your browser origin through CORS. Cookie-based cross-origin requests require explicit allowed origins and credential support. Set withCredentials only when your endpoint uses cookies.
Do not place access tokens in URLs or committed code. Apply download limits and access controls at your backend. Source arrays must contain only files or only URLs, not both.

pages.title: Annotation persistence
pages.lead: Capture a snapshot and restore it with the same study.

blocks.text:
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { DicomViewer } from '@saqif/vue-dicom-canvas'
import '@saqif/vue-dicom-canvas/style.css'
const source = ref('/sample.dcm')
const annotations = ref(null)
</script>
<template>
  <DicomViewer :source="source" v-model:annotations="annotations"
    show-annotation-file-controls worker-base-path="/assets/workers/" />
</template>

items: Store the emitted snapshot JSON through your own API, along with the study identifier.
Restore with the matching DICOM source. Invalid references are rejected.
Replacing annotations creates a new undo/redo boundary.
The package does not autosave or connect to a database.

blocks.text: Annotation snapshots can include study metadata. Protect them as study data. This is the package’s versioned format, not Annotorious JSON.

pages.title: Read-only & accessibility
pages.lead: Build review workflows and keyboard-friendly viewers.

blocks.text:
<DicomViewer :source="source" :annotations="savedSnapshot"
  read-only :annotations-visible="true"
  aria-label="Study review" worker-base-path="/assets/workers/" />
Read-only mode blocks viewer-originated annotation changes while preserving navigation, zoom, contrast, and incoming prop restores. Callers using getApp() directly must enforce their own policy.

head: Key
Action
rows: Left / Right or Page Up / Page Down

blocks.text: Shortcuts act only when the viewer region has focus. Controls and editable inputs retain their standard keyboard behavior.

blocks.text: ESM and CommonJS imports are available. Imports are SSR-safe; image rendering runs after the component mounts in the browser. Use independent source and annotation state for each viewer.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.lead: Common integration issues and direct checks.

head: Symptom
Check
rows: Set a visible container height and import the package CSS.
Copy the workers, check worker-base-path, and verify the URL returns JavaScript rather than an HTML fallback.
Check HTTPS, CORS, authentication headers, server availability, and source limits.
Use the matching study, image/frame references, and package snapshot format.
Turn off read-only mode and enable annotations visibility.
Use unique viewer IDs and one shared worker directory.

Vue DICOM Canvas is GPL-3.0-only. DWV workers retain their license and notices. Review these obligations before choosing the component for your application.

This reference covers npm version 2.0.1, which includes example files alongside the compiled exports, workers, and documentation. GitHub keeps the standalone examples and this website source. Check the npm archive contents for the version you install; worker files are runtime assets and must remain available.
The playground uses a generated synthetic study. Files selected from your device are processed locally by the component; this documentation site does not upload them.
